title: The second look
question: V54 names one look at the bond ladder's reinvestment gap, on naming day in 2031; the model behind every cheque figure looks again in January 2033 and tops the reserve up. Does the text's one look carry the cheques, and what is the truest few-word fix? (round 7 beat 2; W-08)
serves: North star 4 (investing knowledge, applied and true); Wharton: Investment Strategy (define a high degree of funding certainty; the reserve's size and initial asset composition)

rounds.name: Kai breaks the test, Tess reads the register

seeds: Does Kai's lock (price the gap as if its interest earned nothing) hold in the 200,000 futures, and what does it cost her flexibility? (Genius Lab, 13:40)
Road A or road B, in words a stranger can say back, inside 497 strict (Writing Room, 16:20)
essence: Our newest IPS says we check the bond ladder's one weak point once, in 2031, but the plan behind it checks twice, again in January 2033.

Kai caught a leak in my first test, which made the gap look four times bigger than it is; fairly measured, with one check a cheque comes up a little short (usually about $1,300) in about 1 future in 25, and with two about 1 in 770.
So the IPS should either name the second check or use Kai's simpler rule, setting the money aside as if the interest earned nothing, which needs no second check at all.
decided: W0 (86.76% / 45.77%) WITHDRAWN: a leak (the range cut's money went back to Laura) and a ratchet in the score (Kai)
W0f: one look 96.01% / 94.39% of futures pay every cheque in full; two looks 99.87% / 99.85% (base / yields 2 pts lower; MODEL)
Near-breach, not breach. Keel's call: reopen IDEA_LEDGER E2 and put the step in the IPS, by road A (P9) or road B (Kai's lock, P8)
The STRIPS reason: WRONG (a zero locks only money already held; locking future coupon rates needs a forward)
Pitch 'a promise': NOT FALSE, TRUE IF read as 'commitment'; the word is ours, not the case's (Tess)
